newsitem.title: USA: AOL jumps on expectations of pact, refunds.
newsitem.headline: AOL jumps on expectations of pact, refunds.

text.p: Shares of America Online Inc jumped on expectations of a pact with 37 attorneys general to be announced later Wednesday, which is expected to include customer refunds, traders and analysts said.
America Online officials were not immediately available for comment, but the Illinois attorney general's office is holding a press conference in Chicago at 1330 CST/1930 GMT.
"I expect it to cost them something," said Abhishek Gami, an analyst with Nesbitt Burns Securities, adding that the settlement will "eliminate a cloud over the stock."
Shares of AOL jumped two to 37-1/4 in active trading.

"I'm looking at the cost of additional refunds; that's got to be a minimal part of this," Gami said. He said he also expects AOL may also incur a cost for more customer service representatives, which may be another element of its pact.
New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco is also holding a press conference Wednesday regarding AOL, his office said, at 1445 EST/1945 GMT, in lower Manhattan.
One industry source said that refunds are expected to be part of the settlement but that it will not be a blanket refund for the entire membership of the eight million AOL subscribers.
Gami said that in the past, AOL's previous legal settlements have not had a big financial impact on the company.

"In the past AOL has done deals in the single-digits," Gami said, referring to deals such as its class action lawsuit settlement last July that analysts estimate cost AOL between $6 million and $7 million, from a suit that alleged that AOL overbilled customers in minute increments.
AOL has been in talks with 20 attorneys general since last week, about their concerns regarding customer complaints about the inability to access AOL since it started unlimited access.

So far, no states have sued AOL, but New York said that it would sue for allegedly deceptive business practices if the ongoing talks broke down. New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco said last Friday that he would sue AOL within five business days if the negotiations broke down.
AOL has also been hit with several class action lawsuits from angry subscribers, who cannot access the service, or have a hard time getting on because of the busy signal problem.
